malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTML file containing JavaScript that, when opened, redirects the user to a phishing site or uses HTML Smuggling to deliver a malware payload.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the HTML attachment, the code executes JavaScript that either redirects the user to a credential harvesting site or constructs and delivers a malware payload (HTML Smuggling), leading to credential theft or malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTML attachments in emails that execute JavaScript to redirect users or deliver files are a common phishing and malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTML attachments should not contain active JavaScript that initiates network requests or downloads files without user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate business workflows use HTML forms or interactive content, but these do not typically perform redirection or file delivery without clear user action.
key_indicators: Use of HTML Smuggling techniques to deliver executables

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit payload leveraging CVE-2023-34362 to execute arbitrary code on MOVEit Transfer servers, often resulting in deployment of Clop ransomware.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (exploit code, shell, or binary payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the vulnerable MOVEit server receives a crafted request, the exploit triggers remote code execution, allowing the attacker to deploy ransomware or exfiltrate data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exploiting a known RCE vulnerability to gain unauthorized access and execute arbitrary code is a hallmark of targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: MOVEit servers should only execute legitimate, authenticated requests; arbitrary code execution is never expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testers may use similar exploits in authorized security assessments.
key_indicators: Unexpected process execution on MOVEit servers
Network connections to attacker infrastructure post-exploit
Deployment of ransomware or data exfiltration tools

execution_context.file_location: authentication endpoint (web portal, RDP, SSH, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Automated script or tool that attempts to log in using a large number of username/password combinations to gain unauthorized access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During authentication attempts, the code systematically tries multiple password guesses for valid accounts, and upon success, gains access to internal systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: High volume of failed login attempts followed by a successful login is indicative of brute force attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal users do not generate hundreds or thousands of failed login attempts in rapid succession.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security teams may perform password audits or penetration tests.
key_indicators: Multiple failed login attempts from a single IP
Successful login after a series of failures
Use of common or default passwords

attack_chain.action: Phishing email with HTML attachment is sent to hospitality staff.
User opens HTML attachment, which redirects to phishing site or delivers malware via HTML Smuggling.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of user credentials or initial malware foothold

attack_chain.action: Threat actor exploits MOVEit RCE vulnerability to gain access to internal systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of ransomware or further lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Automated brute force attacks are used to obtain valid credentials for internal systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent access and potential data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: HTML email attachments with embedded JavaScript or suspicious redirection
Unusual process execution on MOVEit Transfer servers
High volume of failed authentication attempts followed by a successful login
file_indicators: HTML attachments in inbound email with obfuscated JavaScript
Unexpected executable files dropped on MOVEit servers
Log files showing repeated failed logins
network_indicators: Outbound connections from endpoints to known phishing or malware domains
Unusual traffic from MOVEit servers to external IPs
Authentication attempts from unusual geographic locations or IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor inbound email for HTML attachments containing JavaScript or redirection. Inspect MOVEit Transfer server logs for signs of exploitation or unexpected process creation. Track authentication logs for brute force patterns—multiple failed logins followed by a successful one. Correlate network traffic to identify connections to known malicious infrastructure or anomalous destinations.
